title: ReVMap: Vectorized Global Mapping via Connectivity-Aware Local Map Fusion
claim: Prior pipelines reuse priors and merge local predictions without regard to reliability; ours models uncertainty and connectivity in an iterative loop.
layout: 3 panels: two top contrast panels (✗ vs ✓), full-width pipeline below
description: The figure has three panels. The top row has (a) Global-to-Local Map Prediction and (b) Local-to-Global Map Update. Each is split into a dashed gray baseline box and a highlighted box for the proposed approach. In (a) the baseline is deterministic and uses a red-brown arrow. The proposed side is yellow and uncertainty-aware, with blobs along the lane lines. In (b) the baseline is faded and the proposed side is blue-gray with a connectivity arrow. Red ✗ and green ✓ marks sit under the captions. Panel (c) is a full-width beige box titled ReVMap (Ours). It shows a left-to-right flow from sensor data to an uncertainty-aware local map prediction, then to a local map with uncertainty, then to a connectivity-aware global map update. A bottom global-map strip closes the loop with Prior Retrieval and Update w/ Uncertainty arrows. Yellow marks uncertainty and blue-gray marks connectivity.
caption: Comparison of Map Update Paradigms and the ReVMap Framework. (a) Reliability-agnostic prior reuse leads to over-trusting unreliable accumulated elements, whereas uncertainty-aware prediction modulates their influence. (b) Heuristic matching can lead to incorrect map connections, whereas connectivity-guided revision enables more robust integration of local predictions into the global map. (c) ReVMap iteratively constructs and refines the global map through uncertainty-aware local prediction and connectivity-guided global map revision.
abstract: Large-scale annotation of vectorized high-definition (HD) maps is labor-intensive and costly, motivating local-to-global auto-labeling approaches that incrementally construct global maps from local vectorized predictions. However, existing approaches often overlook prediction uncertainty and rely on heuristic map integration, potentially propagating errors and introducing topological inconsistencies. To address these limitations, we propose ReVMap, a reliable local-to-global framework that iteratively refines local map predictions and global map construction through uncertainty-guided prior utilization and connectivity-guided global map revision. Specifically, ReVMap leverages point-wise localization uncertainty to incorporate global map priors into local map prediction, improving robustness against inaccurate prior information. It then predicts local-to-global connectivity and selectively updates the global map through uncertainty-aware fusion based on the reliability of local predictions. By iteratively coupling local prediction and global revision, ReVMap progressively improves both local map accuracy and global map consistency. Extensive experiments on the nuScenes and Argoverse 2 benchmarks demonstrate that ReVMap achieves state-of-the-art performance in both local map prediction and global map construction.
